def _on_system_boot(self, payload: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
        # [353k4] L0 hot path must not touch the logging handler lock or disk I/O.
        #   The three L0 watchdog timeouts all had their [P0-2] stack frames on
        #   self._log(...) inside this method:
        #     PulseSubconscious.py:493 -> BasePulseOrgan.py:376 -> logging.handle
        #     -> self.acquire() -> self.lock.acquire()
        #   The blocking point is the logging handler lock / disk write, not the
        #   hardware probe (camera probing was moved out of L0 in T-113f).
        #   Fix: every boot-time log record is handed to a short-lived daemon
        #   thread, the DEBUG trace line is removed from the hot path, and all
        #   timing data is kept in memory and emitted only once at the end.
        _m353_t0 = time.perf_counter()
        _m353_marks: list = []

        def _m353_mark(_label: str) -> None:
            _m353_marks.append((_label, time.perf_counter()))

        def _m353_log_async(_level, _msg: str) -> None:
            # Hand the record to a daemon thread so the caller never waits on
            # the handler lock or on the disk write.
            try:
                threading.Thread(
                    target=self._log,
                    args=(_level, _msg),
                    daemon=True,
                    name="m353-boot-log",
                ).start()
            except Exception:
                pass

        if self._running:
            return {"status": "already_booted"}
        self._running = True
        _m353_log_async(LogLevel.INFO, "潜意识已激活，好奇心引擎启动（共享记忆版）")
        _m353_mark("activate_log")

        # v17.0: the dream timer is always initialized, it no longer depends on
        #   the camera probe result.
        # T-113f: camera availability is a hardware I/O call, moved to a daemon
        #   thread so boot returns immediately and stays under the 2s watchdog.
        # 342k5: the thread is kept on purpose (see [342去线程] line below),
        #   because _detect_user_presence_async goes through
        #   utils.safe_hw_probe.safe_camera_devices(), an isolated subprocess.
        #   Making it synchronous would push subprocess start plus device
        #   enumeration back into the boot watchdog window.
        with self._state_lock:
            self._user_present = False
        threading.Thread(target=self._detect_user_presence_async, daemon=True).start()
        # [353k4] the former DEBUG trace line is dropped from the hot path and
        #   kept only as an in-memory mark so it stays greppable in reports.
        #   [342去线程] action=reserved line=475
        #   target=_detect_user_presence_async
        #   reason=hardware_probe_subprocess(T-113f)
        _m353_mark("presence_thread")

        # The dream timer is initialized regardless of camera availability.
        # T-114d: imports were hoisted to module level, so the remaining body is
        #   only interval math plus Timer construction plus start(), which does
        #   not block on the import lock.
        _m353_dream_starter = getattr(self, "_start_dream_timer", None)
        if not callable(_m353_dream_starter):
            _m353_dream_starter = getattr(self, "_init_dream_timer", None)
        if callable(_m353_dream_starter):
            try:
                _m353_dream_starter()
            except Exception:
                pass
        _m353_mark("dream_timer")

        _m353_boot_ms = (time.perf_counter() - _m353_t0) * 1000.0
        try:
            self._last_boot_ms = _m353_boot_ms
            self._last_boot_marks = list(_m353_marks)
        except Exception:
            pass
        _m353_log_async(
            LogLevel.INFO,
            "[353k4] boot_ms=%.1f marks=%s" % (_m353_boot_ms, _m353_marks),
        )
        return {"status": "booted", "user_present": self._user_present}
